manufacturer_maintenance_requirements.text: Carlisle's Owner's Manual recommends inspection at least twice a year and after severe storms, with records kept. It states that regular maintenance inspections are necessary for continued warranty service and coverage. Carlisle Continu-Care: annual maintenance by an authorized applicator extends a 20-yr-eligible Total System Warranty by 5 years (30-yr maximum). The owner must enrol within 1 year of completion. FM Global Data Sheet 1-29 recommends semi-annual and post-storm inspection with written records (DS 1-32 was folded into 1-28/1-29). GAF, Johns Manville and Holcim/Firestone warranty clauses were not verified (search budget exhausted).

roof_age_underwriting.text: ISO endorsement CP 10 36 (Limitations on Coverage for Roof Surfacing, introduced in ISO's 2012 filing) lets insurers value roof surfacing at ACV while the rest of the building stays at replacement cost. It can also exclude cosmetic wind/hail damage. Scheduled premises must be listed, and the cosmetic exclusion is not approved in every state. Carriers commonly start restricting coverage around 10-15 years of roof age. Inspections and ACV conversion are common at 15-20 years, and non-renewal or a replacement requirement is common beyond 20-25. These age thresholds come from contractor and residential-focused sources and should be confirmed with PAX's brokers. No quantified premium or deductible differential for roof age or for a documented maintenance program was found in public sources.

maintenance_documentation_effect.note: Qualitative only. Insurers commonly deny roof claims as wear-and-tear or lack of maintenance, and maintenance records rebut that argument. No study was found that quantifies better claim outcomes or premium credits for documented maintenance. The model should present this as a qualitative benefit, not a dollar figure.

valuation.method: Income approach, direct capitalization: value = NOI / cap rate. So an operating-cost saving S that passes through to NOI changes value by S / cap rate.
applies_when: The owner bears the roof expense and it is an operating expense (above the NOI line), e.g. gross or modified-gross leases, or NNN leases where the landlord keeps 'roof and structure'.
Recurring, stabilized savings. One-off or capital items are not capitalized this way.
does_not_apply_or_needs_adjustment: NNN leases where tenants reimburse roof maintenance via CAM: the saving accrues to tenants, so landlord NOI is unchanged (it may indirectly support rent or occupancy).
Owner-occupied buildings: there is no NOI. Use direct cash-flow/NPV savings instead, and do not capitalize.

Roof replacement is a capital expenditure, usually treated below the NOI line (reserves for replacement / CapEx). Deferring replacement shows up as lower reserves or CapEx in a DCF, not as NOI capitalized at the cap rate. Appraiser practice on including reserves above the line varies.
valuation.note: The formula is standard appraisal practice (Appraisal Institute, 'The Appraisal of Real Estate'), but no source could be opened this session because the web-search budget ran out. Verify wording before client use. Cap rates come from the market files.
